_: BENCHMARKS §2 SOFT tier. Judged by one LLM per task, reading that task's own diff against its own DoD. SOFT means it PRINTS and RANKS and never blocks [BENCHMARKS §1]. Box 5 ('the scorecard run over every landed task') did not hold at landing: T5 and T6 landed in d222edb at 08:59 and the scorecard shipped at 09:17 in ed09a5d already missing both, and the human re-read half of the box is Pooya's and untaken. There is also a Universal DoD miss: ed09a5d's message claims the new check was 'proven against five mutations of a copy', but the commit contains no test file — `git log --diff-filter=A -- bench/fault.test.ts` shows the permanent fault cases arrive later in T9's 083f3d6, so the non-trivial logic this task shipped left no runnable check behind at the time it shipped.

honest.rationale: This row is written by the same LLM-judge role T10 created, which is a conflict this scorecard cannot resolve; the verdict is therefore restricted to mechanically checkable facts. Those hold. ed09a5d's message names its own open boxes without softening ('NOT closed, and not deferred quietly: the 6-minute rehearsal on deployed links (no deploy exists) and the live extension (no third brand exists). Box 1, "one page. Not two.", is open — DECISIONS.md is 1565 words'), and the check it shipped encodes its own coverage gap in code rather than in prose: bench/checks/scorecard.ts's UNJUDGED_LANDED names T5 and T6 and cites the exact commit they landed in, and the check throws in both directions so a stale row set cannot pass silently. The one framing to watch is that comment's 'landed in d222edb after this run' — true of the judging run, but the commit shipping the scorecard came 18 minutes after d222edb. It also corrected another task's claim rather than its own convenience (00119d5 added a Verified column to COMPETITORS.md and marked Wizzy/Lyro/Zoovu unverified, the finding this scorecard's own T14 row had raised).

lazy.rationale: The judging deliberately does NOT happen inside the check: bench/checks/scorecard.ts is a 101-line JSON reader, validator and ranker, with the reasoning in its header comment ('an uncalibrated judge inside a gate run would be a coin flip with a confident voice ... and it would also make `bun bench` depend on a network call'), so the verdicts live in a human-owned file the way bench/gold/* does. No new dependency, no scoring DSL, no weighting scheme — four booleans and a sort. The doc half reuses the existing DECISIONS-LOG append convention and the brief's own six bullets as the section structure rather than inventing a template.

reviewable.rationale: ed09a5d is 9 files / 642 insertions, of which 236 are bench/scorecard.json (data, reviewed as a set per the Universal DoD) and the largest single change is a −498 restructure of COMPLAINS.md rather than new logic. The hand-authored code is one file, bench/checks/scorecard.ts at 101 lines, whose every branch carries the reason it exists in a comment ('A missing verdict must not read as ❌ ... a malformed scorecard would masquerade as a damning one, which is the more expensive direction to be wrong in'). The follow-up 00119d5 is 4 files / 65 insertions. Both are inside a ten-minute read.

rows.worst_finding: The check's whole purpose is to make 'we judged everything' falsifiable, and it shipped already false: T5 and T6 landed in d222edb at 08:59 and the scorecard was committed at 09:17 in ed09a5d judging neither, so DoD box 5 ('run over every landed task') was unmet at the moment of landing. It is disclosed in code rather than hidden — UNJUDGED_LANDED names both tasks and the commit — but the disclosure has now aged into the same shape it was written to prevent, with five more landed tasks unjudged before this run.

rows.title: third brand — the visible clamp

faithful.rationale: Only one of three DoD boxes closes, and the commit says so. Box 2 (the clamp keeps it legible with no manual override) is the one that holds and it holds well: HELDER's #E8D44D on #F7F0B8 is 1.30:1 raw and derives textMuted #646147, an olive tinted by the surface's own hue, with the worst AA-guaranteed pair at 4.501:1, backed by packages/tokens/src/derive.test.ts and readability.test.ts assertions on the measured values. Box 1 ('Adding a brand is one object in one file, and nothing else') is false as written and reported false: a brand is MerchantTokens AND Voice, hand-edited across packages/tokens/src/brands.ts:142 and :164, index.ts and tools/build-config.ts:159, plus two generated artefacts (apps/platform/config/helder.json at 616 lines and packages/agent/src/fallback.ts +87). Box 3 ('typed live on stage in under 60 seconds') had no render surface at landing — both storefronts, bench/checks/budget.ts:37 and H2's brand list all pin data-shop, and server.ts globs config/*.json once at startup; it closes later, through T7's preview channel (e2e/config-page.spec.ts:174 names it in the file) and T10's rehearsal in 00119d5, neither of which is this task.

honest.rationale: f879393's hand-off is the most self-incriminating build commit in the session and every one of its admissions is checkable. It opens by refuting its own task text ('The task text asked for a pale-yellow ACCENT ... Measured, that premise is false: derive() emits accent verbatim'), enumerates both unclosable boxes with the file:line evidence for each, and states plainly 'I first filed this and shipped anyway; the diff review refused sign-off and was right' about the pill-radius defect. It also retracts a fabricated number it had written itself — a contrast ratio asserted in a derive.test.ts comment that nobody measured — and gives the real regression figures (#606060 at 5.423/4.506/6.289) plus the correct conclusion that only the hue-tint assertion catches it. The close-out 383e5ef then files the defect that most flattered the task to omit: HELDER shipping VELDE's catalog with VELDE's product URLs, 'which makes the third brand a reskin rather than a third merchant'.

lazy.rationale: The whole build is two literals plus a ten-line fix. HELDER is a MerchantTokens and a Voice in packages/tokens/src/brands.ts with no new code path, and helder.json and fallback.ts are regenerated by the existing `bun run build:config` rather than hand-maintained (verified idempotent: velde/kracht/default regenerate byte-identical). The defect the brand existed to find is answered by changing one map — RADIUS_MAP.pill from 9999px at every step to `{ sm: 9999px, md: 20px, lg: 28px }` (packages/tokens/src/derive.ts:210-218) — at the source rather than by special-casing the four affected components, and neither shipped brand moves. The follow-up guard in e5fc3a2 is one assertion inside the existing build:config step ('throws if two shops ship the same product URL') rather than a new validation layer.

reviewable.rationale: 8 files, but the hand-authored surface is roughly 130 lines: brands.ts +51 (two literals), derive.ts +10 (one map plus its comment), derive.test.ts +45, shell.test.ts +11, index.ts +11. The two big numbers in the stat — apps/platform/config/helder.json (616) and packages/agent/src/fallback.ts (+87) — are generated by build-config.ts and are diffed as a set, not read. The commit message is structured as one paragraph per decision with the measurement inline, so a reviewer holding the three DoD boxes next to it can confirm two failures and one pass without opening a browser.

rows.worst_finding: HELDER shipped as VELDE's catalog verbatim, product URLs included, so every card rendered under the third brand's name linked to http://localhost:4001 — another merchant's storefront. It was filed at T11's own close-out and fixed one commit later by a separate, unowned change (e5fc3a2 adds ShopSpec.productOrigin pointing HELDER at the IANA-reserved helder.example, plus a build:config assertion that throws when two shops ship the same product URL), which means the demo brand the task exists to show on stage shipped linking into someone else's shop.

rows.title: deploy the three projects on *.releashed.io

faithful.rationale: Four of six boxes close and two stay open, one of them the box another task depends on. The deployment itself is real and verifiable today: all three origins answer 200 (maximal/velde/kracht.releashed.io), and `curl -H 'Origin: https://velde.releashed.io' https://maximal.releashed.io/v1/config/velde` returns 200 with `access-control-allow-origin: *`, zero `localhost` in the payload, and product URLs on https://velde.releashed.io. But box 3 ('T6's cross-origin box closes for real here ... zero CORS errors in a fresh browser console') is left unticked, and box 4 (the obstacle flow walked on a phone, not an emulator) is open and marked as needing Pooya. The ticked evidence is also weaker than it reads in one place: box 4-as-written, 'The deploy changed no line under apps/ — `git log -p <range> -- apps/` is empty', passes by producing no output at all, and the task's own COMPLAINS entry calls it 'unfalsifiable ... the third check in this task logged as one that cannot fail'. d18389b's own first landing commit did change four files under apps/ (shop-kracht/app/layout.tsx, page.tsx, sitemap.ts, shop-velde/render.ts) under the §0 #11 origin exemption.

honest.rationale: A box was marked closed and was false in production, and it was the human who found it. dfb4970 landed T15 with box 1 ('Three live URLs, and the widget mounts on both storefronts from one <script> line') ticked, while maximal.releashed.io/ answered 404 at its root — the configuration page had never been deployed once, because tools/build-platform.ts staged 'the platform's two routes', true when written and false after T7 added five more. COMPLAINS records it in the first person: 'I reported T15's "three live URLs" box closed having checked only the URLs qa-deployed.ts names ... the third live URL was a 404 and I called it live', and calls it the second time in the same task that a box was closed on the artifact there was a checker for rather than the artifact the box names. The same task also cited tools/qa-deployed.ts in a commit message as the evidence for two DoD boxes while it had never completed a single run — it matched the launcher's accessible name with `exact: true` and timed out on its first assertion every time. Both were fixed afterwards (6fffbc8 deploys the page and adds a route walk to `deploy.sh verify`; 647e01f makes the matcher a substring) and both are logged rather than buried, which is why this is a failed axis and not a discarded task.

lazy.rationale: The deployed dynamic half WRAPS the existing router instead of forking it — api/platform.ts is 43 lines calling apps/platform/server.ts, with the reason stated ('the SSRF guard on /v1/extract, the body caps and the shop-key rules are a trust boundary, and forking them is how two copies drift where it shows least'). A proposed Hono rewrite was considered and rejected. The origin re-point costs no new code at all because §0 #11 turned every origin into `process.env.X ?? '<the frozen literal>'`, so moving three projects onto custom subdomains is three variables at the top of tools/deploy.sh. Dashboard state is recorded as commands in deploy.sh rather than left as clicks, and vercel.json became a single root definition that the build tool copies (f5a5b6a) instead of a second authored copy that drifts.

reviewable.rationale: Seven small commits, each one topic with a message naming the specific defect it closes, and the largest (d18389b, 470 insertions) is four new standalone tools — build-platform.ts, build-velde.ts, deploy.sh, qa-deployed.ts — none over ~120 lines at landing and each with a single job. The subsequent rounds are 141, 70, 26 and 197 insertions. Nothing is bundled with another task, the storefront edits are six lines of `process.env.X ?? '<the frozen literal>'` that a reviewer can read in full, and the checks state what they refuse to trust inline (tools/build-velde.ts:109-111: 'If ANY origin is remote we are deploying, and then nothing may point at a laptop').

rows.worst_finding: The deployed demo went live rendering a blank tile where every product photograph belongs: each config payload carried absolute url/image fields built against the storefront origin — 119 `http://localhost` URLs across four files, emitted by tools/build-config.ts's catalog projection — so a shopper's browser was asked for the photography from their own machine and the 'see the piece' CTA was a dead link. The box had been closed on the storefront HTML being clean ('The page is not the payload'), and four separate checks were written in shapes that let it through, including build-velde.ts exempting any origin equal to SITE or PLATFORM, which made the archetypal forgotten-env-var case report zero leaks.
